questions.question: Which statement best describes social determinants of health?
choices: Only a patient’s personal lifestyle choices
Nonmedical conditions and systems that influence health, functioning, and quality of life
A replacement for medical assessment
Information that should not be documented
questions.explanation: Social determinants of health include conditions such as economic stability, access to care, education/health literacy, neighborhood conditions, and social/community context. They influence whether a plan can be completed safely.

questions.question: What is the most respectful way to begin a social-needs screen?
choices: Assume barriers based on the patient’s appearance or neighborhood
Normalize the questions, explain why they matter for care, ask permission, and use plain language
Ask only when the patient misses an appointment
Avoid asking because social needs are not clinical issues
questions.explanation: A universal, normalized, permission-based approach reduces stigma and avoids assumptions. The purpose is to identify barriers relevant to a safe care plan.

questions.question: What does teach-back primarily assess?
choices: Whether the patient agrees with the clinician
Whether the patient can explain the plan and return precautions in their own words
Whether the patient has a high reading level
Whether a family member is present
questions.explanation: Teach-back checks whether communication was clear and exposes gaps in the plan. It tests the explanation, not the patient.

questions.question: Why can a portal-only message be unsafe for an important abnormal result?
choices: All portal messages are inaccurate
Portal release does not prove that the patient received, understood, or acted on the result
Patients are not allowed to view results
Only specialists can communicate results
questions.explanation: Digital access, language, literacy, and ability to use the portal vary. Important results need closed-loop communication and a documented follow-up plan.

questions.question: A patient cannot arrange transportation for urgent evaluation and reports worsening dyspnea and dizziness. What is the safest FNP response?
choices: Tell the patient to keep trying to find a ride
Reassess stability and use an emergency pathway if waiting is unsafe
Close the referral because transportation is a social issue
Schedule routine follow-up in several weeks
questions.explanation: A barrier can change clinical disposition. Worsening symptoms may make an urgent outpatient pathway unsafe and require emergency evaluation.

questions.question: Which action best reflects health equity in FNP care?
choices: Giving every patient the identical plan regardless of barriers
Using assumptions about groups to predict adherence
Identifying and reducing barriers so patients can pursue an appropriate, patient-centered plan
Avoiding preventive care discussions with patients who have limited resources
questions.explanation: Equity means a fair opportunity to achieve health. It requires patient-specific, accessible care rather than identical plans or stereotypes.

questions.question: What is the best next step after a positive screen for a social need?
choices: Document it without discussion
Connect the patient to an appropriate, consented resource and clarify follow-up responsibility
Promise the resource will solve the problem immediately
Remove the medical diagnosis from the chart
questions.explanation: Screening alone does not improve care. A safe response uses an available pathway, respects patient preferences, and closes the loop for high-risk needs.

questions.question: Which situation needs urgent safety action rather than a routine community-resource referral?
choices: A stable patient asking about a food pantry
A patient with immediate danger, serious injury, or suicidal intent
A patient requesting a lower-cost pharmacy
A patient asking for printed instructions
questions.explanation: Immediate danger or medical/behavioral emergency requires an urgent clinical safety pathway. Routine resource referral is not enough in an acute crisis.

questions.question: Why should an FNP avoid labeling a patient “noncompliant” without further assessment?
choices: The label always improves adherence
It can obscure cost, housing, food, language, safety, adverse-effect, or access barriers that require clinical planning
It is required for billing
It means the patient cannot participate in shared decisions
questions.explanation: Judgmental labels can hide the actual reason a plan is not working. A respectful assessment identifies modifiable barriers and supports safer shared planning.

questions.question: What does a closed-loop community-resource referral include?
choices: Giving the patient a website and ending the visit
A reachable resource, understandable instructions, patient consent/preference, and a plan if connection fails
Referring every patient to the same organization
Assuming the patient will call if the need becomes worse
questions.explanation: A closed-loop referral recognizes that resource availability and access may fail. The patient needs an executable plan and the team needs clear ownership of follow-up.
